I remember the excitement and buzz around going to the mall when I was a kid. I remember the local one being pretty busy most of the time. I worked at the Sears for a couple years as one of my early jobs. I'd go check out the independent video game store, chat with my friends who worked at Kay-Bee on my lunch break, make out with my girlfriend who also worked at the Sears for a bit when we had a spare two seconds. The pizza place was awesome. That was the only place in town I could get a good, thin crust, foldable slice. So many businesses that are just gone now: Waldenbooks and B. Dalton, Kay-Bee, Sam Goody, Camelot, Turtle's Records & Tapes, Wolf Camera and Video, Mervyn's. All of these places had locations in this mall.

Then the town went from sketchy, to ghetto, to REALLY ghetto, to one of the worst places in Georgia. The mall, the Toys-R-Us, both theaters, even car lots, closed closed closed. Half the town was closed for years it seemed. Wal-Mart moved, and everything else in that shopping center closed. Now it's all liquor stores, check cashing places, bail bonds, etc. The mall dwindled away, and was torn down a few years ago. Georgia being Georgia, there's now a movie studio in its place.

I've been watching Dan Bell's Dead Mall series. It's a really interesting exploration of the decline of these places.
